response.evidence: At created_suspended, the checkpoint acquires the same estate dispatch.lock used by set_dispatch and compares the full state with admitted_dispatch. A previously committed Pause changes mode/epoch, so the checkpoint raises before ResumeThread. If the checkpoint acquires first, it holds the lock through ResumeThread until resumed releases it; concurrent Pause fails nonblocking acquisition and cannot commit. Admission persists the consumed turn and request digest before launch, with no cancellation rollback.
response.limitation: Source-only review; regressions were not executed, and host.reconcile is not supplied, so exceptional-path quiescence requires verification. Guarantees cover mediated cooperating launches only, excluding unrestricted parent or host-internal requests; they do not establish whole-session confinement.
response.regression: Use two deterministic schedules. (1) After admission, block at the created_suspended observation before checkpoint lock acquisition; commit Pause, then release the barrier. Assert zero ResumeThread calls, no child execution marker, owned-job quiescence after cleanup/reconciliation, and unchanged admitted count/digest with paused mode and incremented epoch. (2) Block immediately after successful checkpoint lock acquisition/state comparison; attempt Pause and assert dispatch-busy refusal and no state write. Release through ResumeThread and resumed lock release, retry Pause, then cancel the running child and assert quiescence. In both schedules assert the consumed count/digest survive cancellation and replay is refused after returning to running.
